items.title: Emile Barnes and Paul Barnes Interview, 1959-10-01
items.q: Oh by the way, I forgot to mention one more man in King Oliver's band. I hate to leave him out. Clarence Black.

ctx.x: Yeah. Which he tells about all those times when they didn't get paid hardly anything. Some nights and now they...

Well anyway, in 1932 I was around New Orleans. I wasn't doing anything much around there. So I met my cousin, who's Baptiste. He said, my son Alex Ruschon is out in Lake Charles. He said, they got a good band out there. He said, why don't you go out there with them? Because Alexis had asked for me. He was a saxophone. He was my scholar and he was a good saxophone player. So I told him, I think I will. I'd go on out there. So I goes on out to Lake Charles. And I joins with that band. And they call it the…

items.title: Paul Barnes Interview, 1969-06-16
items.q: Now, Clarence Black, when I first went out there, Clarence Black is the director. And he would do the paying off.

ctx.x: The second track of Paul Vaughn, Reel 1, June 16, 1969. We're talking about paying off, huh, Baron? Oh, yeah. Yeah, I was asking you, who used to pay off the band to do it with Joe Oliver?

Joe Oliver never pays off himself. He always had someone who wanted to take that. Now, Clarence Black, when I first went out there, Clarence Black is the director. And he would do the paying off. He tend to have been.
